newsitem.title: CANADA: China poultry ban not impacting Canadian exports.
newsitem.headline: China poultry ban not impacting Canadian exports.

text.p: China's ban on poultry infected with a virus has not curbed Canadian exports since the ban was announced Friday, Agriculture Canada said.
"Canada continues to export commercially raised live poultry, hatching eggs and meat to China," an Agriculture Canada statement said.
One cormorant in southern Ontario died in October of Newcastle Disease, or pathogenic avian influenza, Ag Canada senior trade policy analyst Gary Koestler said.
"No commercial poultry operations were affected by this case. Monitoring has uncovered no further cases," the agency said.
China's ban, first made public in the official Chinese newspaper China Daily on Friday, extended to poultry from Canada and the Netherlands.

Canada and China recently signed a revised health protocol requiring exporters to certify that poultry comes from "an area free of disease" at least 50 km (30 miles) from a location where the disease was confirmed, Ag Canada said.
Canada exported C$5.6-million worth of poultry to China so far in 1996. China was Canada's fourth largest poultry export market after the U.S., Cuba and Russia, Ag Canada said.
